## What it is

A copy of `shoe_box_lid`, split off so the two can be adjusted
independently. The lid for `boxes`: slips down over the box's outside
walls by the lid depth, gripped by friction rather than a snap or
thread.

## Design notes

Its length, width and wall must match the box's values or the fit is off;
they aren't shared automatically, so a resize on one side needs the same
change on the other. `fit_gap` is the per-side clearance between the lid's
inside and the box's outside — loosen it if the lid binds, tighten it if
it falls off.

It's modelled cap-down with the open side facing up, the same shape as an
open box, purely so it prints flat with no bridging. Flip it over to use
it as a lid.

The four vertical corners are rounded (`corner_radius`, 10mm by default)
so the first layer's peel front is a curve instead of a point; the plan
footprint is over the 20,000mm2 size where sharp corners warp.

A hole passes straight through the middle of the lid's top, capped at
80% of `width`/`length` so a rim of top is always left around it.
`hole_diameter` is its width and `hole_length` its end-to-end length:
keep them equal for a round hole, or make `hole_length` bigger to
stretch it into an oblong slot. Set `hole_diameter` to 0 to shrink it
away entirely and leave the top solid.

## Don't

- Don't model this cap-up/open-down: that orientation bridges the whole
  top across the hollow interior, which is well past what this printer
  can span without sagging.
- Don't chamfer the inside corners: excluded from polish on purpose, same
  reasoning as the box.
- Don't drop `corner_radius` below 8mm: the warp check will flag it again.
- Don't size the outer shell as `length + 2*wall`: that only leaves room
  for the lid's own wall and the fit gap, not the box's wall as well, so
  the cavity comes out 2*wall too small per side and the lid won't go
  over the box at all. It has to be `length + 4*wall` (box's wall, then
  the fit gap, then the lid's own wall, doubled per side). Checked by
  building both parts into one scene and intersecting them — a spec-only
  read of the numbers didn't catch it, the boolean did.
- Don't add a text-choice parameter (a `hole_shape` of "round"/"oblong"
  was tried on the original before this split): the viewer's sliders only
  carry numbers, so a string default never gets a control and stays
  invisible on screen. Use two numbers instead, as `hole_diameter`/
  `hole_length` do.

## Changelog

- Split off from `shoe_box_lid` as its own part, carrying over that
  part's full history: the cap-down reorientation, the rounded corners
  for warp, the corrected outer-shell sizing, the through hole and its
  `hole_diameter`/`hole_length` controls, and the 80%-of-footprint cap
  with starting values chosen so the sliders can reach it.
